p: Even if your CAT visit is a booked course or group trip, the surrounding area is so good it's worth stretching your stay. Machynlleth has a claim to fame all of its own: Owain Glyndŵr held a Welsh parliament here in 1404, and the historic Parliament House on Maengwyn Street tells the story of Wales's last native Prince of Wales. The ornate clock tower in the middle of town is the obvious meeting point.

Art lovers should look in at MOMA Machynlleth, a gallery and arts venue in a converted chapel, while families might prefer a short drive north to Corris, home to King Arthur's Labyrinth, an underground adventure in old slate caverns, and the little Corris Railway.

Wildlife fans are spoilt too. The Dyfi Osprey Project at Cors Dyfi nature reserve, just outside town, has been a magnet for birdwatchers keen to spot these huge fish-eating raptors during the breeding season. Head west along the estuary and you'll reach the sand dunes at Ynyslas and the long beach at Borth.
Bring proper waterproofs whatever the forecast says. This is lush green country for a reason.

Fancy a souvenir with a conscience? Machynlleth's independent shops lean nicely towards local, handmade and eco-minded goods, which feels about right after a day spent learning how to live a bit lighter.
